docs.title: giFBA: Greedy Interaction Flux Balance Analysis
docs.text:
giFBA is a COBRApy extension for simulating metabolic exchange in microbial communities. Instead of solving one large compartmentalized LP for the whole community (cFBA) or a single joint objective (MICOM), giFBA iterates: each organism is optimized independently against a shared environmental pool of metabolites, only secreted fluxes update that pool, and the process repeats until the community reaches a fixed point, periodic attractor, or until the maximum number of iterations is reached.

The repository contains the gifba Python package (in package/) plus the notebooks, validation models, and analysis scripts used to develop and benchmark it. The comparison against dynamic FBA is described in dFBA Benchmark.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
pip install "git+https://github.com/m-3-lab/giFBA.git@main#subdirectory=package"

See Installation for optional extras and a development setup.

import cobra as cb
from gifba import gifbaObject

model_a = cb.io.load_json_model("organism_a.json")
model_b = cb.io.load_json_model("organism_b.json")

community = gifbaObject(
    models=[model_a, model_b],
    media={"EX_glc__D_e": -10},   # negative flux = uptake available in the shared pool
    rel_abund=[0.5, 0.5],
)

env_final, org_final = community.run_gifba(n_iterations=50, method="pfba")

print(community.summarize())          # per-organism uptake/secretion report
edges, nodes = community.summarize().to_cytoscape()  # export for Cytoscape network viz

Or load one of the bundled toy models:

from gifba import gifbaObject, utils

models, media = utils.load_simple_models("3_1_crossfeed")
community = gifbaObject(models, media)
env_final, org_final = community.run_gifba(n_iterations=25, method="pfba")

docs.title: Package overview
docs.text:
• gifba.gifbaObject: build a community from a list of cobra.Model objects and a shared media, then call .run_gifba() to solve for a fixed point.
  • gifba.CommunitySummary: returned by gifbaObject.summarize(). Formats per-organism and community-level uptake/secretion, and exports Cytoscape node/edge tables.
  • gifba.utils: validation/coercion helpers used by gifbaObject, the bundled toy-model loader (load_simple_models), minimal-medium search (find_min_medium), and optional MICOM/compartmentalized-model interop.

Full details are in the API Reference.

docs.title: gifba.gifbaObject
docs.text:
gifbaObject(models, media, rel_abund='equal', **kwargs)

A microbial community simulated with greedy interaction FBA.

Wraps a list of cobra.Model instances (deep-copied on construction) and runs the giFBA fixed-point loop over a shared media. Can be used as a context manager (with gifbaObject(...) as community:), which is currently a no-op passthrough.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default models Model | list[Model]

The organism model(s) in the community. Deep-copied internally.

required media dict[str, float] | str | list | None

Shared exchange media. A dict maps exchange IDs to fluxes (negative = uptake available). "complete" or None opens every exchange to -1000. A [base_media_dict, min_growth_float] list derives a minimal medium via utils.find_min_medium.

required rel_abund str | array - like

Relative abundance per model. "equal" (default) splits evenly; otherwise a 1D array-like of length len(models), normalized to sum to 1.

'equal'

Other Parameters:

Name Type Description threshold float

Convergence tolerance. Defaults to 1e-12.

oc_rounding int

Decimal places used when checking overconsumption. Defaults to config.ROUND (6).

oc_method str

Overconsumption-correction algorithm, "optim" for a scipy-based LP-optimization approach or "newton" for a Newton-Raphson approach. Defaults to "optim".

community_id str | None

Optional label for the community, used by utils.prepare_compartmentalized_model*.

debug bool

Verbose per-iteration/per-rerun debug printing - primarily included for development purposes. Defaults to False.

verbose bool

Print Iterations/convergence progress and overconsumption progress. Defaults to False.

Attributes:

Name Type Description models list[Model]

The (copied) community models.

media dict[str, float]

Resolved media dict after validation.

num_models int

Number of organisms in the community.

rel_abund ndarray

Resolved relative abundance column-vector, shape (num_models, 1).

objective_rxns dict[int, str]

{model_index: objective_reaction_id} for each model's linear objective.

simulation_count int

Running count of LP solves that cleared the minimum growth cutoff.

env_fluxes DataFrame

Full media flux history, indexed by Iteration, columns are exchange IDs. Index 0 indicates based media for system. Set by run_gifba.

org_fluxes DataFrame

Full per-organism flux history, indexed by (Model, Iteration), columns are reaction IDs. Iteration 0 indices indicate growth/fluxes on the base media - iteration n simulates growht on the n-th iteration media of env_fluxes Set by run_gifba.

iter_converged int | None

Iteration where convergence/periodicity was detected, or None. Set by run_gifba.

periodicity int | None

Length of the detected attractor cycle (1 = true fixed point), or None if no convergence detected. Set by run_gifba.

exchange_ids list[str]

Unique exchange IDs across the whole community. Set by create_vars.

reaction_ids list[str]

Unique reaction IDs across the whole community. Set by create_vars.

exchange_to_metabolite_id dict[str, str]

Exchange ID to metabolite ID lookup, used for reporting. Set by create_vars.

metabolite_id_to_name dict[str, str]

Metabolite ID to name lookup, used for reporting. Set by create_vars.

model_names dict[int, str]

{model_index: model.name}. Set by create_vars.

docs.title: run_gifba
docs.text:
run_gifba(n_iterations: int, method: Literal['pfba', 'fba'], threshold: float | None = None, attractor_size: float | None = None, relaxation_ratio: float | None = None, fp_method: Literal['picard', 'relaxation'] | None = None, verbose: bool = False, debug: bool = False) -> tuple[pd.Series, pd.DataFrame]

Run giFBA for a given number of iterations on the community of models with the given media.

[Flow / Hierarchy] Call create_vars() to initialize storage variables for the simulation. Call _update_media() for each iteration to simulate growth at each discrete step and update state variables in accordance with fixed point iteration-based solver method. See _update_media() for more details. Check fixed point convergence by comparing current iteration to all previous iterations to identify fixed points/periodic behavior. Upon completion/convergence, call average_periodicity() to perform element-wise average of state variables in fixed point/period/attractor.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default n_iterations int

Maximum number of iterations to run the simulation.

required method str

The FBA method to use for the simulation - must be "pfba" (recommended) or "fba".

required threshold float

The numerical threshold for convergence. Defaults to 1e-12 if None provided.

None attractor_size float

The size of the attractor (in percentage of number of iterations) if convergence is not achieved. For a 10 iteration simulation, an attractor of size 0.9 would correspond to averaging over the last 9 iterations. Defaults to 0.9 if None provided.

None relaxation_ratio float

Ratio value chosen for relaxation method used in fixed point solver. Defaults to 1.0 if None provided. Ignored when fp_method is "picard".

None fp_method str

The fixed point solver method to use for the simulation - must be "picard" or "relaxation" (recommended). Defaults to "relaxation" if None provided, so relaxation_ratio still applies. "picard" is relaxation with relaxation_ratio forced to 1.0. "anderson" is reserved and not yet implemented.

None v bool

Toggle verbose output. True will provide printed outputs for current iteration and any re-runs from overconsumption adjustment. Defaults to False.

required debug bool

Development mode. True will provide additional debugging information detailing the simulation process (media & org. fluxes at each step, overconsumption ratio, overconsumption adjustment). Not recommended for real-world community models. Defaults to False.

False

Raises:

Type Description NotImplementedError

If fp_method is "anderson". Raised before any solving starts.

State Modified (Side Effects): self.env_fluxes (pd.DataFrame): Full environmental fluxes DataFrame for all iterations and runs. Multi-indexed by iteration and run, with columns as unique exchange reaction IDs for the entire community (size=(n_iterations, n_exchanges)). (runs currently unused and part of future development). Units in ( mmol/(gT * hr) ). self.org_fluxes (pd.DataFrame): Full organism fluxes DataFrame for all iterations and runs. Multi-indexed by model, iteration, and run, with columns as unique (internal and exchange) reaction IDs for the entire community (size=(n_iterations*n_models, n_reactions)). (runs currently unused and part of future development). Units in ( mmol/(gT * hr) ). self.periodicity (int): Period of the system if convergence is achieved. If convergence is not achieved, this will be None. self.iter_converged (int): Iteration at which convergence is achieved. If convergence is not achieved, this will be None.

Returns:

Type Description tuple[Series, DataFrame]

A tuple containing two pandas objects for simulation steady-state fluxes: - pd.Series: Media/Environment fluxes ($f_{n,j}$) at steady state in units of ( mmol/(gT * hr) ). Size=(n_exchanges,). Returns fixed points, average of periodic fixed points, or average of last * if convergence is not achieved. - pd.DataFrame: Per-organism fluxes ($V_{i,j}$) at steady state in units of ( mmol/(gT * hr) ). Size=(n_models, n_reactions). Returns fixed points, average of periodic fixed points, or average of last * if convergence is not achieved. Calls

  • self.create_vars()
  • self._update_media()
  • self.average_periodicity()

create_vars(m_vals=[1, 1])

Initialize storage for state variables, set initial media, and extract pertinent community details.

Called automatically at the start of run_gifba; only call directly if you need a freshly-initialized community without running it.

[Flow / Hierarchy] Setup method. Called at the beginning of the simulation before the iterative fixed-point solver begins.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default m_vals list[int]

Currently unused; reserved for future package development. Defaults to [1,1] representing each iteration uses 1 input run to modify 1 output run, per iteration. Standard giFBA currently only uses 1 run per iteration.

[1, 1]

State Inputs (Attributes Used): self.media (dict[str, float]): The baseline media conditions for the community. Keys are exchange IDs and values are fluxes (which must be negative). self.models (list[cb.Model]): A list of all Cobra models present in the community. self.n_iterations (int): The total number of iterations to run for the simulation. self.num_models (int): The total number of models in the community.

State Modified (Side Effects): self.env_fluxes (pd.DataFrame): Full environmental fluxes DataFrame for all iterations and runs. Multi-indexed by iteration and run, with columns as unique exchange reaction IDs for the entire community. Size is (n_iterations, n_exchanges). Units are mmol/(gT * hr). self.org_fluxes (pd.DataFrame): Full organism fluxes DataFrame for all iterations and runs. Multi-indexed by model, iteration, and run, with columns as unique (internal and exchange) reaction IDs for the entire community. Size is (n_iterations * n_models, n_reactions). Units are mmol/(gT * hr). self.exchange_to_metabolite_id (dict[str, str]): Mapping of exchange reaction IDs to their corresponding metabolite IDs. self.metabolite_id_to_name (dict[str, str]): Mapping of metabolite IDs to their human-readable names (or exchange reaction IDs). self.exchange_metabolites (list[cb.Metabolite]): A list of all Cobra Metabolite objects across the community. self.exchanges (list[str]): A list of all unique exchange reaction IDs in the community. self.exchange_ids (list[str]): A list of organism-specific exchange reaction IDs. self.biomass_exchange_ids (list[str]): A list of all unique biomass exchange reaction IDs in the community. self.model_names (dict[int, str]): A mapping of the community model index to its string model ID.

docs.title: average_periodicity
docs.text:
average_periodicity()

Average the flux history over the detected attractor.

Averages env_fluxes/org_fluxes over the detected period, or, absent convergence, over the last attractor_size fraction of iterations with a printed warning. Called automatically at the end of run_gifba.

Returns:

Type Description tuple[Series, DataFrame]

(env_flux_avg, org_flux_avg), the averaged media fluxes indexed by exchange ID and the averaged per-organism fluxes indexed by model.

docs.title: gifba.CommunitySummary
docs.text:
CommunitySummary(community: gifbaObject, *, element: str = 'C')

Uptake/secretion summary of a finished giFBA run.

Built by gifbaObject.summarize(). Formats a community's final fluxes into human-readable uptake/secretion tables, at both the whole-community and per-organism level, with optional elemental-flux weighting. str(summary) and repr(summary) return to_string(); in a Jupyter notebook the summary renders as HTML tables.

The tables always describe community.org_final, the fluxes averaged over the detected attractor (or over the trailing iterations when the run did not converge). There is no per-iteration view; use community.org_fluxes for the full history.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default community gifbaObject

A community that has already been run with run_gifba.

required element str

Chemical element (as in cobra.Metabolite.elements) used to compute %-of-flux breakdowns. Keyword-only. Defaults to "C" (carbon).

'C'

Attributes:

Name Type Description flux DataFrame

Long-form per-organism flux table indexed by (Model, Exchange), with Flux, Metabolite, {element}-Number and {element}-Flux columns. Zero fluxes are dropped.

total_flux DataFrame

The same columns aggregated across the whole community, indexed by Metabolite.

objective_rxns dict[int, str]

{model_index: objective_reaction_id}, copied from the community.

objective_vals list[float]

Final objective (growth) flux per model, in model order.

objective_total float

Sum of all models' objective fluxes.

method str

The FBA method ("pfba" or "fba") the community was run with.

iter_converged int | None

Zero-based iteration at which convergence was detected, matching the Iteration labels in community.org_fluxes. None if the run hit its iteration limit without converging.

periodicity int

Number of iterations averaged into the final fluxes: 1 for a fixed point, the cycle length for a periodic attractor, or the trailing window size when the run did not converge.

n_iterations int

Iteration limit the community was run with.

docs.title: find_min_medium
docs.text:
find_min_medium(community: gifbaObject | None = None, models: Model | list[Model] | None = None, base_media: dict[str, float] | None = None, min_growth: float | None = None) -> dict[str, float]

Derive a minimal medium that supports growth of every model.

Runs cobra.medium.minimal_medium on each model with base_media added as sinks, then takes the per-exchange maximum across models, unioned with base_media. Pass either a community or explicit models/base_media/min_growth.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default community gifbaObject

Community whose media is a [base_media, min_growth] list. Its models are used directly.

None models Model | list[Model]

Models to use when no community is given. They are copied, so the caller's models are untouched.

None base_media dict[str, float]

Exchange IDs to fluxes always included in the medium. Signs are ignored. Defaults to an empty medium.

None min_growth float

Minimum growth each model must reach. Defaults to 0.1.

None

Returns:

Type Description dict[str, float]

Media dict of negative (uptake) fluxes keyed by exchange ID.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If neither community nor models is given.

prep_micom_cfba(community_id, ids, paths, rel_abund=None)

Build a compartmentalized cFBA model from a MICOM community.

Requires the micom extra. The objective is the abundance-weighted sum of each organism's biomass reaction.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default community_id str

ID given to the returned cobra.Model.

required ids list[str]

Organism IDs, used as suffixes on MICOM's reaction IDs.

required paths list[str]

Abundance per organism. Defaults to an even split.

None

docs.title: prepare_compartmentalized_model
docs.text:
prepare_compartmentalized_model(community: gifbaObject, rel_abund: list[float] | ndarray | None = None, obj_rxn_ids: list[str] | None = None) -> tuple[cb.Model, list[cb.Reaction]]

Build a compartmentalized cFBA model from a giFBA community.

Each organism gets its own compartments (c1, e1, c2, e2, ...) and e0 is the shared pool, so the result can be compared against giFBA. The objective is the unweighted sum of the organisms' objective reactions. The community's models are copied first and are left unchanged.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default community gifbaObject

Community providing the models, media and community_id.

required rel_abund list[float] | ndarray

Abundance per organism, flat or shaped (n_models, 1). Defaults to community.rel_abund.

None obj_rxn_ids list[str]

Reaction IDs (after renaming) to use as the objective. Defaults to every per-organism biomass(e...) reaction.

None

Returns:

Type Description tuple[Model, list[Reaction]]

(comp_model, objective_reactions).

docs.title: prepare_compartmentalized_model_with_micom
docs.text:
prepare_compartmentalized_model_with_micom(gifba_community: gifbaObject, model_paths: list[str], media: dict[str, float] | None = None, rel_abund: list[float] | ndarray | None = None, obj_rxn_ids: list[str] | None = None) -> tuple[cb.Model, list[cb.Reaction]]

Build a compartmentalized cFBA model from MICOM's reaction set.

Requires the micom extra. Same idea as prepare_compartmentalized_model, but the reactions come from a MICOM community built from model_paths, with internal reaction bounds copied from the giFBA models. The organisms are named Org1, Org2, ... so every per-organism reaction ID carries a __Org{i} suffix.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default gifba_community gifbaObject

Community providing the models, objective reactions, abundances and community_id. It is not modified.

required model_paths list[str]

Model file paths, in the same order as the community's models.

required media dict[str, float]

giFBA-style media, e.g. {"EX_A(e)": -10}. Converted to MICOM's EX_A_m form and applied to the shared exchanges; exchanges not listed are closed to uptake. Defaults to MICOM's medium, which is taken from the model files' exchange bounds.

None rel_abund list[float] | ndarray

Abundance per organism. Defaults to gifba_community.rel_abund.

None obj_rxn_ids list[str]

MICOM reaction IDs (with the __Org{i} suffix) to use as the objective. Defaults to each organism's objective reaction in gifba_community.

None

Returns:

Type Description tuple[Model, list[Reaction]]

(comp_model, objective_reactions). The objective is the abundance-weighted sum of objective_reactions, matching MICOM's community growth rate.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Run from the repository root (the suite takes about 3 seconds):

python -m pytest package/tests               # full suite
python -m pytest package/tests -k validators  # solver-free subset
python -m pytest package/tests -x -q          # stop on first failure

CI (.github/workflows/tests.yml) runs the same suite on Python 3.10 and 3.13 with GLPK on every push and pull request.

  • tests/conftest.py pins the LP solver to GLPK. The golden values were measured under GLPK, and CI has no Gurobi license, so do not remove the pin.
  • tests/golden_values.py holds measured reference fluxes for the ten toy models. Treat a change there as deliberate: re-measure rather than hand-edit, and explain in the commit message why the numbers moved.
  • New tests should cover behaviour that works today. Known defects are tracked separately rather than encoded as xfail.

docs.title: Docstrings and autodoc
docs.text: Public modules, classes and functions should have Google-style docstrings and static type hints. The API Reference is generated from these docstrings by mkdocstrings, so a change to a public docstring shows up on the site at the next deploy. Members starting with _ are left out. To document a new public module, add a ::: gifba.<module> block to docs/api.md.

docs.title: Building the docs
docs.text:
pip install mkdocs-material "mkdocstrings[python]"
mkdocs serve           # live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build --strict  # fail on broken links or missing pages

.github/workflows/docs.yml deploys the site to GitHub Pages on every push to main.

docs.title: AI usage
docs.text: Parts of this repository — including portions of the code, tests, and this documentation — were drafted & implemented with the assistance of AI coding tools (Claude Code). All AI-assisted contributions are reviewed by the project maintainers, and the underlying scientific method, model validation, and numerical results (e.g. unit testing) are checked against expected biological/mathematical behavior rather than taken on faith from generated output.

docs.title: Toy models
docs.text:
Walkthroughs of giFBA on the ten bundled two-organism toy models. Each case name can also be loaded directly with utils.load_simple_models(case).

Interaction Notebook Non-interacting 1_1_single, 1_2_single, 1_3_parallel Competition 2_1_competition Cross-feeding 3_1_crossfeed, 3_2_layered Combined interactions 4_1_crossfeed_competition, 4_2_superfluous_crossfeed Coupling 5_1_coupling, 5_2_dynamical

Bifurcation analyses for the coupling cases are in 5_coupling/bifurcation_analysis/.

Notebooks applying giFBA to AGORA2 GEMs communities:

The AGORA2 models are large binaries fetched separately and are not version controlled.

docs.title: dFBA benchmark
docs.text: A comparison of giFBA against a clamped-biomass dynamic FBA implementation. See dFBA Benchmark.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install "git+https://github.com/m-3-lab/giFBA.git@main#subdirectory=package"

Requires Python 3.10–3.13. Core dependencies (cobra, numpy, pandas, scipy) are installed automatically and give you the full run_gifba path on cobra's bundled GLPK solver.

docs.title: Optional extras
docs.text:
# Faster LP solver via optlang (needs a Gurobi license)
pip install "gifba[gurobi] @ git+https://github.com/m-3-lab/giFBA.git@main#subdirectory=package"

# MICOM interop: utils.prep_micom_cfba / utils.prepare_compartmentalized_model_with_micom
pip install "gifba[micom] @ git+https://github.com/m-3-lab/giFBA.git@main#subdirectory=package"

micom is imported lazily inside those two functions only, and gurobipy is never imported by the package itself; it just lets optlang find Gurobi.

docs.title: Development install
docs.text:
Clone the repo and install editable with the test extras (add gurobi,micom if you need them):

git clone https://github.com/m-3-lab/giFBA.git
cd giFBA
pip install -e "./package[test,gurobi,micom]"
python -m pytest package/tests

See Contributing for testing conventions.

docs.title: dFBA Benchmark: Clamped-Biomass Dynamic FBA
docs.text:
Code, data and analysis live in Examples/2_real_models/4_dfba_benchmark/.

This directory aims to compare how giFBA compared to dFBA, as giFBA is a steady state method for emergent metabolic interactions from dynamic FBA - when held at a constant relative abundance. This directory benchmarks several factors for the following purposes:

  • Defining when giFBA is analogous to dynamic FBA
  • Understanding what dFBA hyper-parameters best match giFBA
  • Benchmarking efficiency differences in giFBA vs dFBA

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
4_dfba_benchmark
 ┣ 4_*.ipynb                  Analysis notebooks
 ┣ process_results.py         Raw JSON (from HPC runs) -> processed CSVs
 ┣ benchmark_analysis_utils.py # Utils for seamlessly plotting and reviewing results
 ┣ vacc_scripts/              Cluster scripts that ran the simulations
 ┗ data/
   ┣ AH_BI/, N_orgs/          Processed tables (csv, pkl)
   ┗ raw/                     Zipped raw results

Requires plotly, seaborn, tol_colors and matplotlib on top of gifba.

docs.title: Experiments
docs.text:
This directory was used to simulate multiple configurations:

  • AH BI only communities - This community showed a curious interaction so exploration was done as a baseline for the method before implementation on communities with more models. Models simulated using a glucose-limited media.
  • N_orgs comparing communities with 1-10 models to benchmark efficiency and identify dfba parameters which affect equivalence with giFBA.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The simulations were run on the UVM VACC with the scripts in vacc_scripts/, which write one JSON file per run. Those results are zipped in data/raw/ (Benchmark_AH_BI.zip, Benchmark_N_orgs.zip); unzip them in place to reprocess (unzip data/raw/Benchmark_AH_BI.zip -d data/raw/). The unzipped folders are gitignored. The VACC scripts write to a relative Benchmark_* folder on the cluster, so their paths are not tied to this layout.

Each result stores the following information:

  • Number of organisms
  • List of Model Names of each GEM in the community
  • List of Relative abundances of each GEM in the community
  • y0_factor: Since media is stored as a flux, this defines how much each media component's concentration is scaled up/down from the original magnitude of flux - this only affects metabolites in the media, components not present in the base media remain 0. This hyperparameter was only implemented for the AH BI community.
  • y0_offset: This is a flat value used to offset the concentrations calculated. This amount is added to the media component's concentration only if it is present in the base media. This hyperparameter was only implemented for the AH BI community.
  • Sum_N_rxns: Sum of the length of all the reactions in the community (ignoring duplicates across organisms) as an analogue for the complexity of each community
  • Sum_N_mets: Same as the reactions, but summed across the metabolites
  • vmax and km: michaelis menten kinetics values. Each metabolite is assumed to have exactly these same identical constants.
  • solver_method: the chosen method for solving the dfba simulation, using scipy solve_ivp. May be either "BDF" or "RK45" to understand which solver may be faster.
  • early_stop_window and early_stop_tol: dfba is considered converged once the concentrations are linear over time. This is done by running a linear regression after each time step. The window defines the number of points used for the regressor. The stop tolerance defines the threshold for the sum of squared residuals in order to be considered sufficiently linear. When a model is considered linear, the dfba simulation is halted.
  • model_solver: generally listed as "glpk". This tracks what solver is used to solve each LP in the GEMs. "glpk" is slower, but used since gurobi implements limits on the number of parallel simulations allowed.
  • gifba_solve_time and dfba_solve_time: The wall clock time required to solve the respective simulation types. This is stored only after the simulation converges/completes.
  • gifba_pfba_calls and dfba_pfba_calls: The number of times pfba is solved (each technique simulates each organism at least 1 time per iteration/time step). This is a stronger display of efficiency compared to wall clock time, due to wall clock time's dependence on the computer
  • dfba_status: logs the current number of pfba calls while dfba is simulating. This is kept in case the method times out on the UVM VACC, then the number of calls can still be recorded and used - the wall clock time will simply be replaced with the timeout length in analyses (24 hrs)
  • error: this is in case a simulation fails for development purposes to see why it failed - other lines may be added in this case, but primarily for development only
  • status: this logs the status of the simulation for tracking where the simulations are at each time step. This will match dfba_status during dfba runs, but will state if params are loaded, models are loaded, if gifba was simulated, etc. Generally ignorable
  • gifba_fluxes & dfba_fluxes: a dataframe turned to a dict (for json compatibility) for the flux of each reaction in each microbe for the respective method. This is used to compare accuracy

docs.title: Benchmark Analysis
docs.text:
process_results.py loads the raw JSON once and writes the processed tables to data/{AH_BI,N_orgs}/ (hyperparams_*.csv, model_names_*.csv, fluxes_*.pkl). Run it from the benchmark directory:

cd Examples/2_real_models/4_dfba_benchmark
python process_results.py                  # every experiment
python process_results.py --config AH_BI   # one experiment

The notebooks read those tables and save figures to Examples/figures/real_model_figs/dfba_benchmark/:

  • 4_1_compare_hyperparameters.ipynb: wall clock and pFBA-call efficiency, and MAE/RPE against the dFBA hyperparameters
  • 4_2_compare_fluxes.ipynb: reaction-level giFBA vs. dFBA flux comparison
  • 4_3_pca_comparison_AH_BI.ipynb: PCA of giFBA and dFBA fluxes for the A. hallii / B. infantis community (needs a local AGORA2 install set in agora_dir_base, plus the .mat models in ../data/)

Set ACTIVE_CONFIG_NAME at the top of 4_1/4_2 to switch between experiments.

The aim of this subdirectory is to be able to use this data to inform how dfba and gifba compare answering a form of the question: "giFBA is a steady state method for estimating a dfba solution, but what kind of dfba simulation is it efficiently solving?"
